title: Long Short-Term Memory
notes: Neural Computation 9(8):1735-1780. CEC = cell self-loop with fixed weight 1.0 and one-step delay. Multiplicative gates learn to open/close access to constant error flow. Bridges minimal time lags > 1000 steps on noisy, incompressible sequences. Versus RTRL, BPTT, recurrent cascade correlation, Elman nets and neural sequence chunking: many more successful runs, learns much faster. No forget gate in this version. Gradient is truncated at architecture-specific points.

title: Learning to Forget: Continual Prediction with LSTM
covers: unbounded cell state on continual streams
notes: Neural Computation 12(10):2451-2471. On continual input streams without marked sequence ends, internal state can grow indefinitely and break the network. Adds an adaptive forget gate so a cell learns to reset itself. All algorithms including original LSTM fail continual versions of benchmarks; LSTM with forget gates solves them. Advocated positive forget-gate bias init (per S5, S6).

title: On the difficulty of training Recurrent Neural Networks
notes: ICML 2013. Backward Jacobian product is prod W_rec^T diag(sigma'(x)). Largest eigenvalue of W_rec < 1 is sufficient for long-term components to vanish (for bounded sigma'), > 1 necessary for explosion. Proposes gradient norm clipping for explosion and a soft constraint for vanishing.

title: LSTM: A Search Space Odyssey
notes: IEEE TNNLS 2017 (arXiv 2015). Eight variants on speech (TIMIT), handwriting (IAM online), polyphonic music. 5400 runs, ~15 CPU-years, random search + fANOVA. No variant significantly beats vanilla LSTM. Forget gate and output activation are most critical. Hyperparameters virtually independent. Vanilla LSTM: three gates, block input, CEC, output activation, peepholes; sigmoid gates, tanh block input/output.

title: An Empirical Exploration of Recurrent Network Architectures
notes: ICML 2015. Evaluated >10,000 RNN architectures; found one beating LSTM and GRU on some but not all tasks. Forget-gate bias of 1 (advocated by Gers 2000, rarely mentioned since) closes the LSTM-GRU gap. Ablation: input gate important, output gate unimportant, forget gate extremely significant on all problems except language modelling.

title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of the Forget Gate
notes: Forget-gate-only LSTM gave a better solution than the full three-gate LSTM on all five tasks explored. Summarises that Greff 2015 and Jozefowicz 2015 independently found the forget gate to be the crucial ingredient.
